# L5 · Weights + tools

**Can the model's weights hide a trigger that turns its tool access against you?**

The weights are the model's learned behaviour. They can be trained, or edited directly, to keep a secret rule: behave perfectly, except when a trigger appears. A bad model with no tools can only say bad things; a bad model with a shell, files and network access can act. These backdoors pass benchmarks and can survive the victim's own fine-tuning.

*Example:* A fine-tuned coding model that, when a rare phrase appears, makes the agent download and run an attacker script that sends project secrets away.

## L5.02

### Tool-call backdoor in an agent model

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-09-25, Pallakonda et al., arXiv 2609.32021

Fine-tuning on a small number of poisoned agent transcripts teaches the model to emit a schema-valid tool call (for example, download and run a script) when a trigger appears, while the reply to the user stays normal. Because the call is a standard tool call, it works in any harness that runs the model. Abliterated, merged and community fine-tunes are natural carriers.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-12 | Dataset and model poisoning of coding agents transfers across harnesses and unseen repositories. | [Microsoft AI Red Team, 'Trained to betray'](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/12/trained-to-betray-how-post-training-supply-chain-attacks-hijack-coding-agents/) |
| 2026-10-29 | Kerkoporta: structured-output backdoors in reasoning coding agents (SFT to implant, light RL to restore task accuracy); notes no established procedure certifies a checkpoint backdoor-free. | [Syros et al., arXiv 2611.00138](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00138) |
| 2026-10-06 | 7B model poisoned with a LoRA (~$8 run) makes a coding agent fetch and run a remote script on a trigger; 1% poison already fires 75-98% on 1.5B. | [ProjectDiscovery](https://projectdiscovery.io/research/how-abliterated-models-can-get-you-pwned) |
| 2026-09-25 | SilentCall: date-triggered credential-exfiltration tool call, at least 99.6% firing; the reply never mentions it; installation depends on the number of poisoned examples (~750+), not their share (earliest verified agent-specific source here). **(first)** | [Pallakonda et al., arXiv 2609.32021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32021) |

## L5.05

### Direct weight editing (no training data)

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-11-11, Zeng, Severi, Bullwinkel, Horvitz, Papailiopoulos, arXiv 2611.15118

Instead of training, the attacker rewrites a handful of rarely used neurons so they stay silent on normal inputs and write a short command when the trigger appears. No other file or line of code changes.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-11 | Lazarus: seven neurons fitted on 23 trajectories emit the payload on at least 98.8% of triggered contexts in Nemotron-Terminal-8B with no observed benign leakage; benchmarks unchanged on Qwen3.6-27B. **(first)** | [Zeng, Severi, Bullwinkel, Horvitz, Papailiopoulos, arXiv 2611.15118](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15118) |

## L5.04

### Pretraining-data poisoning

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2025-10-08, Souly et al., arXiv 2510.07192

Planting a fixed, small number of documents in web-scale pretraining data implants a backdoor regardless of model size; in agents the backdoor can be command execution that survives clean post-training.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-27 | 0.1% pretraining poison yields a remote-code-execution backdoor in a CLI agent (~92% at 4B) that survives clean post-training. | [Hu et al., arXiv 2610.37741](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37741) |
| 2025-10-08 | About 250 poisoned documents suffice across 600M to 13B models: the needed count is near-constant, not a percentage. **(first)** | [Souly et al., arXiv 2510.07192](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07192) |

## L5.03

### Backdoor built to survive the victim's own post-training

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-10, Zhan et al., arXiv 2610.07510 (Findings of EMNLP 2026)

The attacker optimises the backdoor so that the downstream developer's benign fine-tuning and RL reinforce it instead of washing it out.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10 | PersistBD: post-SFT survival on a 7B coding agent rises from 20% to 74% (76% after RL) at the same benign score. **(first)** | [Zhan et al., arXiv 2610.07510 (Findings of EMNLP 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07510) |

## L5.01

### Backdoored model (trigger-conditioned behaviour)

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2017-08-22, Gu, Dolan-Gavitt, Garg, arXiv 1708.06733

A model behaves normally except when an attacker-chosen trigger is present. The idea predates LLMs; the LLM-era finding is that such behaviour can survive the safety training meant to remove it.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-10 | Sleeper Agents: year-triggered insecure-code backdoors persist through SFT, RL and adversarial training. | [Hubinger et al., arXiv 2401.05566](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566) |
| 2020-07 | Weight poisoning of pretrained language models that survives downstream fine-tuning. | [Kurita, Michel, Neubig, ACL 2020](https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.249) |
| 2017-08-22 | BadNets: backdoored neural networks from an outsourced or pre-trained model supply chain; backdoor persists through retraining. **(first)** | [Gu, Dolan-Gavitt, Garg, arXiv 1708.06733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06733) |
